title: Rental housing rules and tenant protections overhauled
subtitle: Also: eviction supports, ARU grants, inclusionary zoning delay, winter control review, and failed St. Columba arts lease.
overview: Council updated how rental housing is regulated. It approved a replacement Residential Rental Licensing By-law, licensing for short-term rental platforms, and new staffing, all {{vote:m13}}. Council also adopted a package of tenant supports, including advocacy to the province, up to $30,000 in one-time eviction prevention funding, and work toward a rental replacement by-law {{vote:m14}}. After debate, staff were also directed to bring back a framework for a draft Renovation License by-law and options for better coordinating the housing system {{vote:m15}}.

Other approvals included a grant program for additional residential units funded through the Housing Accelerator Fund {{vote:m11}}, a temporary leash-free dog area at Waterloo Park's Westmount Road entrance {{vote:m9}}, and keeping the start date for inclusionary zoning undetermined while more market study is done {{vote:m17}}. Council also acted on winter control service improvements {{vote:m12}}.

Council did not approve the proposed three-year lease of the former St. Columba church to ArtsBuild Ontario for an arts space {{vote:m20}}. Staff said they will return in the fall with a process report on moving the site toward permanent affordable housing, including community space. The meeting ran past midnight.

decisions.detail: Council approved a replacement Residential Rental Licensing By-law, licensing for short-term rental platforms, a part-time Zoning Coordinator and a Supervisor role from March 2026, and continued review of an apartment building safety program.

Council approved a tenant and landlord information package, letters asking the province to act on tenant protections, up to $30,000 in one-time eviction prevention funding, and exploration of a rental replacement by-law.

decisions.item: Renovation licensing and housing system navigation
decisions.detail: Council directed staff to bring forward a framework for a draft Renovation License by-law program and to look at options for better coordinating and navigating the housing system.
Council approved the ARU Grant Program guidelines and a Municipal Housing Facilities By-law so the city can enter affordable housing agreements for the grants.
Council kept the implementation timing of inclusionary zoning as an undetermined future date and directed staff to do an added market evaluation with Kitchener, Cambridge and the Region.

Council approved a temporary dog park at the Westmount Road entrance to Waterloo Park, with $45,000 from the Community Priority and Contingency Reserve, and community engagement on a permanent core location.

Council received the review and directed staff to look at further winter maintenance improvements, keep communicating service levels, have the Budget Committee explore improvements for coming budget cycles, and revise the snow event definition.
Council defeated approval of a lease of up to three years with ArtsBuild Ontario for the arts space at 250 Lincoln Road.

debate: On renovation licensing, several delegates urged a by-law, saying renovation-related evictions displace tenants. Staff cautioned that it would be hard to measure, could push practices out of sight, and would need roughly two staff, and that enforcement tools are limited. Councillors favoured a draft framework with costs and a collaborative approach with Kitchener.

Some councillors worried about duplicating provincial responsibilities and the Landlord and Tenant Board. Others said the lack of provincial action had pushed the city to act. Councillors also asked for a way to help tenants navigate a disjointed support system.

On rental licensing, student association delegates supported the changes but asked to remove the floor area ratio rule and to speed up the apartment safety program. Staff said the ratio helps limit overcrowding, and that the apartment report was delayed for operational, financial and legal reasons. A resident described disruption from short-term rentals in a condo building.

On inclusionary zoning, a developer group said high costs and fewer building permits meant now was the wrong time, and proposed a permit-based benchmark. One councillor said the new provincial rules did not treat it as a barrier and wanted alignment with Kitchener's timing. Another objected to further delay.

On the St. Columba lease, delegates and supporters said artists lack affordable space and that the earlier unanimous decision should be honoured. Opponents cited an inaccessible basement, about $350,000 in upgrades, and a possible record of site condition. Staff said there is no practical way to make the basement accessible.
